newsitem.title: INDIA: India call easy, excess funds may seek gilt route.
newsitem.headline: India call easy, excess funds may seek gilt route.

text.p: Indian call money rates opened lower at 0.25-0.75 percent on Thursday against the previous close of 0.50-1.00 percent, dealers said.
Call money was quoted 0.25-0.50 percent in latest trade, dealers said. "It likely to fall further," a dealer said.

The Reseve Bank of India's announcement of 14-day treasury bills will act as a benchmark and a refernce rate for interbank term money and 14-day repo money, a dealer said. "The 14 day treasury bill will yield in the region of 4.75-5.00 percent on June 6," a bank dealer said.
Thursday's repo auction will see more bidders at a lower cut-off, a state-run bank dealer said.
"The cut-off rate may fall to 3.75-4.00 percent against the previous 4.22 percent," he said.

The securities market will see action as bankers will rush to park their excess money in the short to medium term securities, while those who have already taken positions will try to sell securities to book profit, a dealers said.
